texts: A parliamentary system is a form of government in which the executive branch is drawn from the legislature and depends on its support to stay in power.
A parliamentary system is a form of government in which the executive branch, the prime minister and cabinet, is drawn from the legislature and depends on its support to stay in power.
Voters elect members of parliament, and the party or coalition holding a majority of seats forms the government.
The prime minister is the head of government, while a separate head of state, such as a monarch or a president, performs mainly ceremonial duties.
Parliament makes laws, approves the budget, and questions ministers.
If parliament passes a vote of no confidence, the government must resign or call a new election.
This differs from a presidential system, where the president is elected separately and cannot be removed simply by losing a legislative vote.
India, the United Kingdom, Canada, and Germany are examples of parliamentary democracies.
